1na
m. [ts], the sound ‘n’ ; the consonant ‘n’; Sadd 604,.20 (ta tha da dha na); 661,.13 (sabbanāmassa takārassa nattaṃ hoti vā sabbaliṅgesu); 774,.1 (nassa saddassa tappurisabahubbīhisu uttarapade attaṃ hoti); —    °-kāra1,    m., 1. the letter or sound ‘n’; Ja III 15,5´ (yasassi naṃ paññavantaṃ visayhā ti …tīni p’ etāni ālapanān’ eva, nan ti pan’ ettha nipāto, vyañjana-siliṭṭhatāvasena ~assa anunāsikatā katā ti paccetabbā, Ce so; Ee anunāsikā katā ti; Be ntakārassa sānunāsikatā; Se takārassa anunāsikā paccetabbā); V 80,23´ (paññāvidhā natthī ti ~o padasandhikaro paññāvidhā atthī ti attho); Spk III 291,.21 (na kho n’ etan ti na kho etaṃ, ~o pan’ ettha vyañjanasandhimattam evā ti veditabbo); Th-a III 151,.15 (gāthāsukhatthaṃ ~’-āgamaṃ katvā); Bv-a 258,.4 (~assa ṇādesaṃ katvā, Be, Se so; Ce, Ee omit); — 2. the syllable ‘na’; Ja III 43,.19 (eko dukāram eva bhaṇi eko sakāraṃ eko ~aṃ eko sokāraṃ) ≠ Spk I 142,.17; Ja III 47,.10 (~aṃ vatvā vattukāmassa ayaṃ gāthā natthi anto …).

2na
[ts] (before a following initial vowel there can be hiatus after na, but more usually (a) na + ā̆- before a single consonant > nā-; (b) na + ā̆- before a double consonant > na- or nā-; (c) na + i- before a single consonant > na-y-i-; (d) na + ū̆- > nu-, nū-, no- (influenced by metre or rhythm); (e) na + e- > ne-; — in such cases n’- (as with elision) is often written in Ee; (f) after na a following initial single consonant (from an ‘original’ double consonant) of a verb is often doubled); not; no; nor, neither; Abh 1147 (na a no mālaṃ nahi); Sadd 889,.4 (na no mā a alaṃ halam icc ete paṭisedhanatthe); 904,.10 foll. (na no icc ete padādimhi c’ eva padāvasāne ca nipatanti na padamajjhe … pamatto puriso puññakammaṃ karoti na); Vin I 8,22* (sadevakasmiṃ lokasmiṃ natthi me paṭipuggalo); III 150,.18 (yassa na kkhamati so bhāseyya); 195,.26 (bhagavatā sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ na atirekacīvaraṃ dhāretabban ti); 212,.8 (na mayaṃ āvuso ājīvakā bhikkhū mayan ti); 215,.28 (mahicchā ime samaṇā Sakyaputtiyā asantuṭṭhā na-y-ime sukarā cīvarena acchādetuṃ); 220,.18 (na kiñci avacāsi); 234,.9 (nāñño koci hārako hoti, Be, Ce, Ee so; Se na añño); D II 104,.18 foll. (na tāvāhaṃ … parinibbāyissāmi yāva me bhikkhū na sāvakā bhavissanti viyattā …); 106,.18 (na ciraṃ tathāgatassa parinibbānaṃ bhavissati); 162,.32 (yaṃ na icchissāma taṃ na karissāmā ti); III 47,.11 (so issāmacchariyaṃ kulesu nuppādetā hoti, Be, Se so; Ce kulesu anuppādetā; Ee na uppādetā); M I 179,.13 (na-y-idaṃ sukaraṃ agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā … brahmacariyaṃ carituṃ); 246,.22 (na-y-ito bhiyyo); 426,.15 (hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā); 486,.23 foll. 3na
ind. [ts], like, as, as it were; Ja V 339,24* (yaṃ na … andhena tamasā gataṃ; 341,19´ : yaṃ nā ti ettha nakāro upamāne … gatan ti kataṃ, ayam eva vā pāṭho, purimassa nakārassa iminā sambandho na katan ti kataṃ viyā ti attho); Sadd 889,.10 foll. (na iti upamāne pi vattati yaṃ na … andhe na tamasā kataṃ ettha nasaddaṃ gahetvā kataṃsaddena yojetvā na katan ti padassa kataṃ viyā ti attho bhavati).

4na
ind. [= nu1], interrogative particle; S I 190,.30 (handa dāni bhikkhave pavārayāmi vo na ca me kiñci garahatha kāyikaṃ vā vācasikaṃ vā; Spk I 276,.33 : ettha na ca kiñcī ti pucchanatthe nakāro, kiṃ me kiñci garatha); Ja VI 63,17* (kulaputtarūpo sappuriso na seve, Be, Ce, Ee so; Se nu; 63,21´ : nakāro paripucchanatthe nipāto, Be so; Ce, Ee nakāro paṭipucchanattho; Se nukāro paṭipucchanatthe nipāto); 213,9* (na tena vyāpannarasūdakā na, Be so; Ce, Ee naṃ; Se vyāpannarasūdakāni; 216,3´ : ettha eko nakāro pucchanattho hoti, nanu tena vyāpannarasūdakā nadiyo ti hi taṃ pucchanto evam āha).

6na
mfn., demonstr. pronoun [cf ena, ta(d), Pkt ṇa], he, she, it; (in acc. often following a particle, esp. atha, or at the end of a sentence, after imperat. or fut., and so possibly to be interpreted as particle; cf naṃ2; or functions as an enclitic form of ta(d); naṃ, ne are prob. sometimes in Ee wrr for taṃ, te), Sadd 274,.21 foll. (tasaddassa nāmikapadamālā vuccate: so te naṃ taṃ ne te …); 661,.13 foll. (sabbanāmassa takārassa nattaṃ hoti vā sabbaliṅgesu: naṃ taṃ ne te …); — sg. acc. naṃ1 :Vin I 75,.7 (ayaṃ so kārabhedako coro handa naṃ nemā ti); 207,.38 (ārāmikagāmo ti pi naṃ āhaṃsu); S I 102,29* (idh’ eva naṃ pasaṃsanti); A I 248,.5 (gandhakaraṇḍake vā naṃ nikkhipanti); IV 172,6* (abhinibbajjayātha naṃ); Dhp 1 (tato naṃ dukkham anveti); Sn 139 (na naṃ jāti nivāresi brahmalokūpapattiyā); 1076 (yena naṃ vajju taṃ tassa natthi); 1094 (nibbānam iti naṃ brūmi); Ja I 54,.24 (putto kira te mahārāja jāto passissāmi nan ti āha); 152,.14 (atha naṃ mātā tassa santikaṃ gacchantaṃ disvā); 222,.30 (atha naṃ evam āha); 287,.20 (sace sakkosi mārehi nan ti, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee tan ti); IV 278,19* (jīvaṃ ca naṃ gahetvāna); Vism 314,.30 (saha bhaṇḍena gahitacoraṃ vadhetha nan ti); Ps I 229,.7 (Buddharakkhito sakuṇena gahito mocema nan ti); — pl. acc. ne: Vin I 42,35* (atha ne satthā viyākāsi); IV 44,.9 (handa ne vuṭṭhāpessāmā ti); S I 224,.22 (devā apāyaṃsveva … abhiyaṃsveva ne asurā); A I 132,14* (tasmā hi ne namasseyya, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee te) = It 110,17*; Sn 223 (tasmā hi ne rakkhatha appamattā); 288 (na ne koci nivāresi kuladvāresu); Thī 465 (atha ne bhaṇati Sumedhā; Thī-a 258,.26 : ne ti mātāpitaro); Ja III 204,.18 (pucchissāmi ne ti); 537,.23 (atha ne tittiro kasmā rodathā ti āha, Be, Se so; Ce, Ee te); IV 367,23* (khippaṃ ca ne nimantaya, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee te); V 114,2´ (atha ne tayo pi eka-āḷāhanen’ eva jhāpesuṃ, Ce, Ee, Se so; Be te); 314,.13 (mātāpitaro mamam eva bhārā aham eva ne paṭijaggissāmi); VI 551,29* (ko ne dassati bhojanaṃ; or read no with L. ḍahati
dahati2 (and ḍayhati1 ?), pr. 3 sg. [S. dahati; AMg ḍahai], burns, consumes; torments; Vin I 204,.24 (anujānāmi bhikkhave dhūmaṃ pātun ti … taṃ yeva vaṭṭiṃ ālimpetvā pivanti, kaṇṭhaṃ dahati, Ee so; Ce kaṇṭho ~ati; Be, Se kaṇṭho dahati); II 120,.26 (jantāghare aggi mukhaṃ ~ati); IV 33,.23 (paṭhaviyā paṭhavīsaññī … dahati vā dahāpeti vā); M I 86,.10 (kinti me bhoge n’ eva rājāno hareyyuṃ … na aggi ~eyya, Ce, Ee, Se so; Be daheyya); 333,.26 (ayaṃ samaṇo nisinnako va kālakato handa naṃ ~āmā ti, Se so; Be, Ce, Ee dahāmā ti); 338,25* (sayaṃ ~issasi attānaṃ bālo aggiṃ va samphusaṃ) = Th 1205 (Be so; Ce dahissasi; Ee dahissam; Se ~issati); M I 365,.8 (sa ādittā tiṇukkā hatthaṃ vā ~eyya bāhuṃ vā ~eyya, Se so; Be, Ce, Ee daheyya); III 186,.6 foll. 1dhamma
m. (and n.) [S., BHS dharma], dhamma denotes (an interpretation of) the essential nature and reality of existence and experience, the way things are: it is descriptive and prescriptive; it denotes also an essential attribute of men or animals; a quality or characteristic; Abh 784 (~o sabhāve pariyattipaññāñāyesu saccappakatīsu puññe ñeyye guṇācārasamādhisū pi nissattatāpattisu kāraṇādo); see also Sv 99,.3 foll., Ps I 17,.16 foll., It-a I 37,.20 foll., Paṭis-a 18,.1 foll., Bv-a 13,.4 foll., As 38,.23 foll. and Sadd 560,.25 foll.; — for Buddhists dhamma is used to denote an interlocking and interdependent assembly of concepts: the true nature of the world of experience, how that world works, and the way to transcend it, as understood by the Buddha; the progressive stages of understanding and nibbāna ; the behaviour, the practice, required to achieve understanding of the way the world of experience works, ie the way to reach arhatship, nibbāna ; the understanding and practice taught by the Buddha, the substance of his teaching, the texts of the Canon, especially the Suttapiṭaka ; all constituents of the world of experience, physical and mental, external and internal, progressively more and more minutely analysed; all constituents of prescribed practice, appropriate and beneficial actions; prescriptions for the members of the saṅgha ; — for people generally dhamma is an interpretation of the essential nature of existence and experience; the way one should act, depending on who one is, to maintain the way things are and should be; duty; right; justice; normative and beneficial actions; — 1. (i) how the world of experience works, the processes by which it works and is explained (especially as formulated in cattāri ariyasaccāni and paṭiccasamuppāda ), and the possibility and way of transcending it, as understood by the Buddha and taught by him (so that knowledge and understanding of it might bring enlightenment, arhatship, to others); Vin I 2,3* (yadā have pātubhavanti ~ā ātāpino jhāyato brāhmaṇassa ath’ assa kaṅkhā vapayanti sabbā yato pajānāti sahetudhammaṃ; Sp 954,.19 foll. : pātubhavantī ti uppajjanti ~ā ti anulomapaccayākārapaṭivedhasādhakā bodhipakkhiyadhammā, atha vā pātubhavantī ti pakāsenti abhisamayavasena vyattā pākaṭā honti, ~ā ti caturāriyasaccadhammā); 11,.2 (idaṃ dukkhaṃ ariyasaccan ti me bhikkhave pubbe ananussutesu ~esu cakkhuṃ udapādi); 12,.24 (ehi bhikkhū ti bhagavā avoca svākkhāto ~o cara brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā ti); 15,.31 (idaṃ kho Yasa anupaddutaṃ idaṃ anupassaṭṭhaṃ ehi Yasa nisīda ~aṃ te desessāmī ti); 40,.19 foll.
